sentences.text: Ms. Sharmila Sharma - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri K. K. Tiwari - Govt. Advocate for the respondent/Sta
Heard on I.A. No.3406/2024, which is second application for suspension of jail sentence and grant of bail filed under Section 389 of the Cr.P.C. on behalf of appellant - Akram Khan.

The first application was dismissed on merits vide order dated 07.02.2023.
T h e trial Court has convicted the appellant vide judgment dated 30.01.2018 passed by the Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Shajapur in S.T. No.41/2017 as under:-
Imprisonment in Section & Act Punishment Fine (if deposited) lieu of fine amount 363 of the IPC 3 years R.I. Rs.1,000/- 6 months RI 366 of the IPC 5 years R.I.
Rs.2,000/- 1 year R.I. 376(1) of the IPC 10 years R.I. Rs.5,000/- 1 year R.I. 4 of POCSO ACT, 10 years R.I. Rs.2,000/- 1 year R.I. 3(1)(W)(2) of SC/ST 3 years R.I.
Rs.1,000/- 6 months R.I. ACT 3(2)(5) of SC/ST Life Imprisonment Rs.5,000/- 2 years R.I. ACT A s per prosecution case, on 18.01.2017 at about 7:30 p.m., appellant forcibly took the prosecutrix and committed rape upon her.
The prosecutrix belongs to SC community, while the appellant belongs to other than SC/ST community.
The prosecutrix was recovered on 19.01.2017 from the possession of appellant.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant has not committed any offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.
The age of the prosecutrix is not accessed properly by the trial Court.
Scholar register of Class I of the prosecutrix has not been filed and proved by the prosecution.

The learned trial Court has relied upon scholar register of Class VI of the prosecutrix,
which is not permissible.
It is further submitted that it has not been proved by the prosecution that the appellant has knowingly committed rape upon the prosecutrix that she belongs to Scheduled Caste community.
It is submitted that the learned trial Court without considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case has wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellant.

It is also submitted that the Akram Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149272375/
1 appellant has served incarceration around 07 years, which is more than 50% of the sentence awarded by the trial Court.

sentences.text: Final hearing of the appeal is not possible in near future therefore, it is prayed that remaining jail sentence of the appellant may be suspended and appellant may be released on bail.

Learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent/State opposed the prayer of the appellant by referring Paragraph No.31 of the impugned judgement and submits that learned trial Court has properly given findings that the appellant has knowingly committed rape upon the prosecutrix that she belongs to SC community.
After dismissal of first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail of the appellant, there is no change in circumstances.
Therefore, the application is liable to be rejected.
We have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

Considering the fact that after dismissal of first application for suspension of jail sentence of the appellant, there is no change in circumstances in which this repeat application can be considered.
Resultantly, I.A. No.3406/2024 is hereby rejected.
I.A. No.3407/2024 for urgent hearing also stands closed.
List for final hearing in due course.
(S. A. DHARMADHIKARI) (PRAKASH CHAND  JUDGE JUDGE  Shruti Akram Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149272375/
